 Open Enrollment for ACA Marketplace Is Underway. What to Know About Coverage Options, Rising Premiums
 Shelby Hawkins | November 19, 2026, 7:26 pm 
 Open enrollment is underway for Affordable Care Act health insurance. Overall, the cost of medical insurance is up, and Illinois saw ACA premium increases range from 1.8% to 14.9%, marking the second straight year of a double-digit jump. 
 Employer-sponsored healthcare plans are also expected to rise by 8.2% next year.
 The spikes can be attributed to underlying healthcare costs, according to Gbenga Ajilore, who serves as chief economist at the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities. Those underlying costs include prescription drugs, hospital care and physician services. Inflation impacts those prices.

 “One major factor is that over the last decade, we’ve seen a lot of hospital consolidations and a lot of mergers,” Ajilore said. “That’s caused a lot of increase in prices that gets passed through to insurance on to us.”
 The expiration of enhanced ACA subsidies can also mean significantly higher monthly insurance bills for many Americans.
 Americans just voted in midterm elections and overwhelmingly chose to put Democrats in Congress; many campaigned on lowering healthcare costs. One way lawmakers could facilitate that would be reinstating the premium tax credit enhancements that expired at the beginning of this year.
 Health insurance marketplace enrollment fell by 18% over the past year, according to KFF Health News, resulting in more than 4.6 million Americans losing their coverage. Enrollment through Get Covered Illinois, by contrast, is down 15% this year, marking a loss of more than 92,000 no longer enrolled in ACA health insurance.
 “When people don’t have health coverage, then they usually wait, and they wait until it’s too late, and then it becomes more expensive,” Ajilore said. “At the end of the day, we want everyone to be covered and able to have access to health coverage.”
 Having more people opt out of health insurance can cause a great ripple effect as a decrease in insured people can equate to an increase in premiums.
 “We have seen an influx of folks buying more affordable plans,” said Morgan Winters, director of  Get Covered Illinois . “I think in a lot of cases, that’s a really good move for a consumer because they pay less in premiums per month, but that really is based on your healthcare needs, which is why it’s really important to talk to a professional.”
 Rural communities and older Americans bear the brunt when health insurance prices go up, Winters said, emphasizing counties in southern Illinois that are particularly vulnerable to the surges.
 “The value of health insurance is the peace of mind of knowing that if you have a medical emergency, that you are going to be covered,” Winters said. “Folks are making the decisions between being able to afford groceries and being able to afford health insurance. So it’s really important that they understand how to get the most affordable coverage that meets their healthcare needs.”
 Open enrollment goes until Jan. 15. For coverage to start Jan. 1, enrollment must be completed by Dec. 15.
